newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish left withdraws threat to topple government.
newsitem.headline: Danish left withdraws threat to topple government.

text.p: A Danish left-wing party holding pivotal seats in parliament withdrew on Thursday its threat to help overthrow the minority government over an attempt to block a visit by British author Salman Rushdie.

Socialist People's Party leader Holger Nielsen told the daily Det Fri Aktuelt he was now satisfied that the centre-left coalition acted out of incompetence rather than over a secret political agenda in seeking to put off the trip by Rushdie.
"I now see the case as solely one in which Nyrup and his people have bungled, and a blunder is not something on which we would topple the government," Nielsen said.

Rasmussen's political opponents initially suspected that the government's claim that it could not guarantee Rushdie's security if he went ahead with plans to collect a European Union literary prize could have been an effort to appease Iran.

Rushdie has lived in hiding and under guard since 1989 when Iranian revolutionary leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini issued a fatwa or death sentence against him for his novel "The Satanic Verses", saying it blasphemed against Islam.

Iran is traditionally a major buyer of Danish feta-type cheese, importing 1.2 billion crowns ($207 million) worth in 1991-92, although sales have fallen off of late because of importers' bad debts which Danish producers are trying to recover. ($1=5.797 Danish Crown)
